title: Grain Marketing Contracts: Price Floor Premiums, Accumulation Rates and Desk Service Levels
content:
Three catalogue terms distinguish what a marketing programme of Grain Marketing Contracts sells the member beyond a place to deliver bushels: the premium charged for a price floor, the bushels accumulated each trading week under an accumulator structure, and the level of grain desk support the programme carries.

| Programme | Price floor premium (USD per bushel) | Bushels accumulated each trading week | Grain desk support carried |
|---|---|---|---|
| Spot Cash Delivery Ticket | 0.00 | 0 | scale house handling only |
| Forward Cash Sale Contract | 0.00 | 0 | the standing grain desk |
| Basis Fixed Contract | 0.00 | 0 | the standing grain desk |
| Hedge-to-Arrive Contract | 0.00 | 0 | the hedge desk |
| Delayed Price Agreement | 0.00 | 0 | the standing grain desk |
| Minimum Price Contract | 0.24 | 0 | the hedge desk |
| Managed Accumulator Program | 0.00 | 2500 | a managed programme |

The price floor premium is carried by the one programme in the catalogue that sells a floor, the Minimum Price Contract, at 0.24 per bushel; every other programme carries none. The weekly accumulation figure is carried by the one programme built on an accumulator structure, the Managed Accumulator Program, at 2500 bushels each trading week.

## Illustration on hypothetical bushels

A hypothetical Minimum Price Contract written for 20,000 bushels carries a floor premium of 0.24 on each of them, being four thousand eight hundred dollars for the floor. A hypothetical Managed Accumulator Program accumulates 2500 bushels in each trading week it runs.
